bg.$description: Warm bone — actual paper, not zinc.

bg-elevated.$description: One full step from surface so buttons read as affordances (QA: the old Δ8 was invisible).

control-edge.$description: Outline of interactive controls (buttons, fields, dropdowns, checkboxes, radios, switch tracks, segmented pickers): at least 3:1 on every background, bg-elevated being the worst case. Hairline dividers stay on border.

divider.$description: Short dividers between items in a row: tab-strip tabs, top-bar groups. Between border and control-edge, about 2:1 on the tab strip and the top bar capsule.

text-muted.$description: Information text: at least 4.5:1 on bg, bg-surface, bg-elevated, bg-inset, bg-stripe and bg-canvas. Stays visibly quieter than text-secondary. Disabled controls are exempt.

accent-fill.$description: Fountain ink already carries white text at 7:1.

chart-1.$description: Chart series 1 (Usage: Claude). The series hues are a fixed order validated together for colour-blind separation and at least 3:1 on this palette's cards; colour follows the thing, never its rank.

chart-other.$description: Chart series for anything past the named ones.

status-working.$description: Working marks (the working grid, the Thread strip's dot, starting / installing dots): the highlight colour's legible variant, so they follow the palette's accent and a chosen one. --color-accent-text clears 4.5:1 on bg, bg-surface and bg-elevated (lib/style-accent.ts for a chosen colour), which keeps the marks over 3:1 on selected and hovered rows.

status-ok-soft.$description: Ok text and dots (the (active) mark, ok callouts): at least 4.5:1 on every ground.

status-error-bright.$description: 'Bright' inverts to darkest on light — it's the emphasis step.

row-hover.$description: Hover band on a list row (Settings lists): about 1.3:1 against the resting row on dark palettes, 1.2:1 or more on light ones. On it the row's muted text steps up to text-secondary (SETTING_LIST_ROW_HOVER), which reads at 4.5:1.

media-label-bg.$description: Behind a name or time drawn on video (any picture, either scheme).
